div.head: Ine 40
div.ab: LXXXIIII. Ciorles wurðig sceal beon wyntres ⁊ sumeres betyned; gif he biþ untyned, ⁊ receþ his neahgebures ceap on his agen geat in, nah he æt þam ceape nan wuht: adrife hit ut ⁊ þolie (þone) æfwyrdlan.
LXXXIIII. Ceorles worðig sceal beon wintres ⁊ sumeres betyned; gif he bið untyneð, ⁊ recð his neahgebures ceap in on his agen geat, nah he æt þam ceape nan wuht: adrife hine ut ⁊ ðolie æfwerdlan.

Ceorles þeorðig (id est rustici curtillum) debet esse clausum estate simul et hieme. Si disclausum sit, et introeat alicuius uicini sui captale per suum apertum, nichil inde recipiat, sed educat et patiatur dampnum suum.
{LXXXIIII} Ceorles worðig sceal beon wintres ⁊ sumeres betyned. Gif he bið untyneð, ⁊ recð his neahgebures ceap in on his agen geat, nah he æt þam ceape nanwuht: adrife hine ut ⁊ ðolie æfwerdlan.

A ceorl’s pasturage shall be fenced winter and summer. If it is not fenced, and his neighbor’s livestock strays in through his own opening, he has no claim on the livestock: let him drive it out and suffer the damage [that the livestock did].

A commoner's premises shall be fenced both winter and summer. If they are not enclosed, and a beast belonging to his neighbour strays in through the opening he himself has left, he shall have no claim on that beast, [but] he shall drive it out and suffer the damage.

A ceorl’s homestead must be fenced winter and summer. If it is not fenced, and his neighbour’s cattle get in through his own gap, he has no right to anything from that cattle; he is to drive it out and suffer the damage.

Des Bauern Hofstelle soll Winters und Sommers umzäunt sein; wenn sie nicht umzäunt ist, und seines Nachbarn Vieh dringt ein in seine eigene [die vom Bauern gelassene] Öffnung, so erhält er nichts von diesem Vieh: (sondern) er treibe es aus und leide den Schaden.

The peasant’s homestead is to be fenced winter and summer; if it is not fenced, and his neighbour’s livestock gets in through his own opening [the one left by the peasant], he gets nothing from that livestock: (but) let him drive it out and suffer the damage.
